items.title: Divorce
items.heroTitle: Divorce Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Guiding you through contested and uncontested divorce with clarity, strategy, and steady advocacy.

paragraphs: Facing a divorce is one of the most emotionally and legally challenging experiences you can go through. Whether you are just beginning to consider your options or are already in the midst of a difficult separation, you need an experienced Houston divorce attorney who understands both the legal complexities and the emotional weight of this process. At Hirani Law Firm, we provide the compassionate, strategic legal representation you need to protect your rights, your assets, and your children's future.

sections.heading: Contested Divorce
paragraphs: A contested divorce occurs when spouses cannot reach an agreement on one or more key issues, such as property division, child custody, or spousal support. This type of divorce often requires negotiation, mediation, and potentially a court trial. Having a skilled attorney in your corner is essential to ensure your rights and interests are fully protected throughout this adversarial process.

sections.heading: Uncontested Divorce
paragraphs: An uncontested divorce happens when both parties agree on all terms. While this process is generally less stressful and more cost-effective, it is still crucial to have an attorney review any agreements to ensure they are fair, comprehensive, and legally binding. A seemingly simple agreement can have long-term financial and personal consequences.

sections.heading: Filing & Serving Papers
paragraphs: The process begins with filing a Original Petition for Divorce with the court and formally serving your spouse. Texas requires a mandatory 60-day waiting period before a divorce can be finalized.

sections.heading: The Discovery Phase
paragraphs: Both parties exchange financial information through a formal process called discovery. This is critical to ensure a fair and complete picture of all marital assets and debts, including hidden or undervalued property.

sections.heading: Negotiation & Mediation
paragraphs: Most divorce cases are resolved outside of court through negotiation or mediation. Our firm is skilled at advocating for your interests at the bargaining table to reach a settlement that protects your future.

sections.heading: Trial (If Necessary)
paragraphs: When an agreement cannot be reached, our experienced trial attorneys are fully prepared to present your case before a judge. We prepare every case as if it will go to trial, giving you maximum leverage in negotiations.

sections.heading: Division of Assets & Debts
paragraphs: Texas is a community property state. This means that assets and debts acquired during the marriage are generally owned equally by both spouses. We work to ensure that the division is not just equal, but equitable, fighting against any attempts to hide or undervalue marital property.

sections.heading: Business & Retirement Accounts
paragraphs: Dividing complex assets like business interests, stock options, and retirement accounts (401ks, pensions) requires specialized knowledge. We work with financial experts to ensure these assets are valued correctly and divided fairly.

sections.heading: Spousal Support (Alimony)
paragraphs: Texas has specific and strict requirements for Spousal Maintenance (alimony). We fight to ensure you receive the support you are entitled to, or we work to protect our client from an unfair support obligation.

sections.heading: Child Custody & Conservatorship
paragraphs: In a Texas divorce involving children, the court will establish a Conservatorship arrangement, which defines each parent's rights and duties. We advocate for the arrangement that is truly in your children's best interest and that protects your parental rights.

sections.heading: Child Support
paragraphs: Child support is calculated based on state guidelines tied to the paying parent's net monthly resources. We ensure that child support orders accurately reflect each parent's financial situation and the needs of the children.

sections.heading: A Compassionate Approach
paragraphs: We understand that divorce is more than a legal matter; it's a deeply personal and often painful life transition. We are committed to guiding you through this process with both compassion and clarity.

sections.heading: Experience You Can Trust
paragraphs: Attorney Sehar Hirani has dedicated her career to family law in the greater Houston area. We have the knowledge and experience to navigate even the most complex divorce cases effectively.

sections.heading: Aggressive When It Matters
paragraphs: While we always seek amicable resolutions, we are fully prepared to be your fierce advocate in mediation and in the courtroom when the other party refuses to be reasonable.

items.title: Child Custody
items.heroTitle: Child Custody Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Protecting your relationship with your children through every stage of a custody matter.

paragraphs: A child custody dispute is one of the most emotionally charged legal battles a parent can face. When the relationship between you and your child is at stake, you need more than just a lawyer; you need a powerful, compassionate advocate. As your dedicated child custody attorney in Houston, Hirani Law Firm combines deep legal knowledge of Texas family law with a genuine understanding of the emotional stakes for your family.

sections.heading: Managing Conservatorship
paragraphs: In Texas, 'conservatorship' refers to the legal rights and duties a parent has regarding their child. A 'Managing Conservator' has the right to make significant decisions about the child's life, including decisions about education, healthcare, and religious upbringing.

sections.heading: Possessory Conservatorship
paragraphs: A 'Possessory Conservator' generally does not have the right to make major decisions for the child but has the right to spend time with the child (possession and access / visitation).

sections.heading: Joint Managing Conservatorship (JMC)
paragraphs: This is the most common arrangement in Texas and is presumed to be in the best interest of the child. In a JMC, both parents share the rights and duties of a Managing Conservator. However, one parent is typically designated as the 'primary' conservator with the right to establish the child's primary residence.

sections.heading: Sole Managing Conservatorship (SMC)
paragraphs: A court awards one parent Sole Managing Conservatorship when joint managing conservatorship is deemed not in the child's best interest, which typically requires evidence of abuse, neglect, domestic violence, or substance abuse by the other parent.

sections.heading: The "Best Interest of the Child" Standard
paragraphs: In any custody decision, the court's only consideration is the 'best interest of the child.' This is not about the parents' desires or convenience; it is about what will provide the child with the most stable, nurturing, and safe environment.

sections.heading: Key Factors Courts Evaluate
paragraphs: When determining the best interest of the child, a judge will consider factors such as: the child's age, emotional, and physical needs; the stability of each parent's home; each parent's willingness to support the child's relationship with the other parent; any history of domestic violence or child abuse; and the child's own preferences (if the child is 12 or older, the court must consider, but is not bound by, their expressed preference).

sections.heading: We Listen First
paragraphs: Before we strategize, we take the time to truly understand your family's unique situation, your goals for your children, and your concerns about the other parent.

sections.heading: Strategic, Aggressive Advocacy
paragraphs: We develop a tailored legal strategy designed to achieve your custody goals. If the other party is uncooperative or is attempting to alienate you from your children, we fight aggressively to protect your parental rights.

sections.heading: Focused on the Children
paragraphs: While we are your advocate, we never lose sight of the fact that the ultimate goal is to achieve the best outcome for your children.

items.title: Child Support
items.heroTitle: Child Support Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Establishing, enforcing, and modifying fair child support under Texas guidelines.

paragraphs: Child support is not just a legal obligation; it is a fundamental right of your child. Whether you need help establishing a fair support order, enforcing an order that is being ignored, or modifying an outdated order that no longer reflects reality, Hirani Law Firm provides the dedicated, experienced legal representation you need. As your Houston child support attorney, our focus is always on ensuring your child has the financial security they deserve.

sections.heading: Texas Child Support Guidelines
paragraphs: Texas uses a specific formula to calculate child support, based on a percentage of the paying parent's net monthly resources. The percentage varies by the number of children covered by the order: 1 child = 20%, 2 children = 25%, 3 children = 30%, 4 children = 35%, 5+ children = 40%.

sections.heading: Income & Resources Considered
paragraphs: 'Net monthly resources' is a specific legal definition under Texas law. It generally includes wages, salary, self-employment income, commissions, rental income, and other sources of regular income, minus certain deductions like federal income taxes and Social Security.

sections.heading: Deviations from the Guidelines
paragraphs: A court can order an amount that differs from the guideline amount if applying the standard would be unjust or inappropriate. Factors that can lead to a deviation include the child's special healthcare or educational needs, travel costs for visitation, and the paying parent's ability to pay.

sections.heading: If the Paying Parent Won't Pay
paragraphs: Failing to pay court-ordered child support is a serious matter with serious consequences. If the other parent is not paying, you should contact an attorney immediately. Time matters, as missed payments accrue as judgments.

sections.heading: Legal Tools for Enforcement
paragraphs: We can file an enforcement motion with the court to compel payment. A judge has numerous powerful tools available, including: withholding income directly from the payor's employer (Wage Garnishment), seizing tax refunds and other assets, suspending the payor's driver's and professional licenses, reporting the arrears to credit bureaus, and in the most egregious cases, jailing the non-paying parent for contempt of court.

sections.heading: When Can Support Be Modified?
paragraphs: A child support order can be modified if there has been a 'material and substantial change in circumstances' since the last order was signed. Common triggering events include a significant increase or decrease in either parent's income, a change in the child's medical needs, or a change in the child's primary residence.

sections.heading: The Modification Process
paragraphs: Modifying a child support order requires filing a Petition to Modify and proving the change in circumstances to a judge. We guide you through this process efficiently.

sections.heading: Fighting for What Your Child Deserves
paragraphs: We are tireless advocates for ensuring that child support orders are fair and are actually paid. Your child's needs are our priority.

sections.heading: Experienced Enforcement Counsel
paragraphs: We know how to use every legal tool available to compel a non-paying parent to meet their obligation. We will not let non-compliance go unaddressed.

sections.heading: Clear, Strategic Advice
paragraphs: Whether you are establishing a new order, seeking enforcement, or requesting a modification, we provide clear, strategic advice tailored to your specific family situation.

items.title: Adoption
items.heroTitle: Adoption Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Helping Texas families grow through stepparent, relative, and adult adoptions.

paragraphs: Adoption is one of the most beautiful and life-changing legal processes a family can go through. Whether you are a stepparent looking to formalize your bond, a grandparent or relative stepping in to care for a child, or a family welcoming a child through the foster system, the legal process can seem overwhelming. As your dedicated adoption attorney in Houston, Hirani Law Firm is here to guide you through every step with compassion, expertise, and care, ensuring this joyful journey goes as smoothly as possible.

sections.heading: Stepparent Adoption
paragraphs: The most common type of adoption we handle. If you are a stepparent who has formed a true parental bond with your spouse's child, we help you navigate the process, including obtaining consent from or terminating the rights of the other biological parent.

sections.heading: Adult Adoption
paragraphs: Texas law allows adults to be legally adopted, typically by a stepparent, relative, or someone who served in a parental role. This formally recognizes an existing parental bond and has important legal implications for inheritance and other rights.

sections.heading: Relative (Kinship) Adoption
paragraphs: When a grandparent, aunt, uncle, or other relative becomes the primary caregiver for a child, kinship adoption permanently establishes their legal parental rights, providing stability and security for the child.

sections.heading: Private / Independent Adoption
paragraphs: We assist birth parents and adoptive families in navigating private adoptions, ensuring all legal consents are properly obtained and that the best interests of the child are protected throughout the process.

sections.heading: Foster Care Adoption
paragraphs: Adopting a child you have been fostering through the Texas Department of Family and Protective Services (DFPS) involves a unique set of legal requirements. We help foster families navigate the DFPS process and complete their adoption.

sections.heading: Petition Filing
paragraphs: We prepare and file all necessary legal documents with the court, including the Petition for Adoption.

sections.heading: Home Study
paragraphs: A court-ordered home study evaluates the prospective adoptive family to ensure the child's placement is safe and suitable. We help you understand what to expect.

sections.heading: Consent & Termination
paragraphs: This is often the most complex part of an adoption. We handle all issues relating to obtaining written consent from the biological parent(s) or petitioning the court to involuntarily terminate parental rights when necessary.

sections.heading: Finalization Hearing
paragraphs: The adoption is made final and legal at a court hearing. This is a joyful moment we are proud to share with our clients.

sections.heading: A Joyful Process
paragraphs: We approach adoption with the same joy and dedication you feel. Our goal is to handle the complex legal work so you can focus on welcoming your child into your family.

sections.heading: Legal Expertise
paragraphs: The adoption process involves navigating complex family law statutes and court procedures. Our experience ensures your adoption is handled correctly the first time.

sections.heading: Compassionate Support
paragraphs: We understand the emotional nature of adoption. We provide clear, consistent communication and a supportive presence throughout the entire journey.

items.title: Father's Rights
items.heroTitle: Father's Rights Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Defending fathers who want to remain present and active in their children's lives.

paragraphs: Society has changed, and the law has changed with it. Fathers are no longer seen as secondary parents, and the Texas legal system recognizes that a father's active involvement is critical to a child's well-being. Yet, many fathers still face significant challenges in asserting their parental rights. As your dedicated father's rights attorney in Houston, Hirani Law Firm is a powerful advocate for fathers who want to be fully present in their children's lives.

sections.heading: The Law Is Gender-Neutral
paragraphs: Texas family law is explicitly gender-neutral. A court cannot favor a mother over a father based solely on gender. The standard for all custody and visitation decisions is the 'best interest of the child,' and we use the law's equal footing to fight for your rights as a father.

sections.heading: Rights of Married vs. Unmarried Fathers
paragraphs: Married fathers are automatically presumed to be the legal father of children born during the marriage. Unmarried fathers must take proactive legal steps to establish their paternity and, therefore, their parental rights.

sections.heading: Voluntary Acknowledgment of Paternity
paragraphs: Signing an Acknowledgment of Paternity (AOP) form at the hospital is the simplest way for an unmarried father to establish legal paternity. However, this does not automatically establish custody or visitation rights.

sections.heading: Paternity Lawsuit (SAPCR)
paragraphs: To establish legal rights to custody and visitation, an unmarried father (or the mother) must file a Suit Affecting the Parent-Child Relationship (SAPCR) with the court.

sections.heading: DNA Testing
paragraphs: In contested paternity cases, DNA testing can be ordered by the court to conclusively establish biological fatherhood.

sections.heading: Seeking Joint Managing Conservatorship
paragraphs: The ideal outcome in most cases is to be named a Joint Managing Conservator, giving you equal legal rights to make decisions about your child's life. We build strong cases for joint conservatorship.

sections.heading: Establishing a Fair Possession Schedule
paragraphs: Beyond legal rights, we fight for a possession and access (visitation) schedule that gives you meaningful, regular time with your children.

sections.heading: When the Mother Moves Away (Relocation)
paragraphs: If the other parent is threatening to move your child out of the area or out of state, we act quickly to file for a temporary restraining order and a hearing to protect your access to your child.

sections.heading: If Your Visitation is Being Denied
paragraphs: If the other parent is denying your court-ordered visitation, we file an enforcement motion and pursue all available legal remedies to restore your access.

sections.heading: Modifying Existing Orders
paragraphs: If an existing order doesn't give you fair time with your children, we can file a petition to modify the order based on a material and substantial change in circumstances.

sections.heading: We Believe Fathers Matter
paragraphs: We are genuine advocates for fathers' rights. We believe that children thrive when both parents are actively involved in their lives, and we fight for arrangements that reflect this.

sections.heading: Aggressive, Experienced Representation
paragraphs: We are skilled family law litigators who are not afraid to go to court to protect your parental rights.

sections.heading: Local Court Knowledge
paragraphs: Our experience in Houston and surrounding area courts gives us insight into how to effectively present a father's rights case locally.

items.title: Conservatorship
items.heroTitle: Conservatorship Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Clarifying parental rights, duties, and decision-making for your children.

paragraphs: When a loved one becomes incapacitated and can no longer manage their own personal or financial affairs, the legal process of establishing a guardianship or conservatorship ensures they have a designated person to protect their best interests. This is a serious legal undertaking that requires skilled legal guidance. As your conservatorship attorney in Houston, Hirani Law Firm can guide you through this complex process with compassion and expertise.

sections.heading: Guardian of the Person
paragraphs: A Guardian of the Person has the legal authority to make decisions about the ward's personal life, including where they live, what medical treatment they receive, and their general day-to-day care.

sections.heading: Guardian of the Estate
paragraphs: A Guardian of the Estate (sometimes called a conservator) has the legal authority to manage the ward's financial affairs, including their assets, income, and property.

sections.heading: Full Guardianship
paragraphs: A full guardianship removes all of the ward's legal rights and places full legal authority over the person, the estate, or both, with the guardian. This is ordered when the ward is determined to be completely incapacitated.

sections.heading: Limited Guardianship
paragraphs: A limited guardianship removes only specific rights from the ward and grants the guardian authority over only those specific areas. Courts in Texas favor the least restrictive option that still protects the individual.

sections.heading: Temporary Guardianship
paragraphs: Temporary guardianship can be granted quickly in emergency situations where an incapacitated person faces an immediate risk of harm and a permanent guardianship has not yet been established.

sections.heading: Petitioning the Court
paragraphs: The process begins with filing a formal Application for Guardianship with the appropriate probate court, stating the reasons guardianship is needed and providing information about the proposed ward's condition.

sections.heading: The Investigation
paragraphs: The court will appoint an attorney ad litem to represent the interests of the proposed ward and will conduct an investigation, typically including a medical exam, to verify the need for guardianship.

sections.heading: The Hearing
paragraphs: A hearing is held before the probate court, where evidence of incapacity is presented. If the court finds that guardianship is necessary, it will appoint a guardian.

sections.heading: Ongoing Duties
paragraphs: Guardians have ongoing legal obligations, including annual reporting to the court on the ward's status and the management of their assets.

sections.heading: Protecting Your Loved One
paragraphs: Our primary goal is to ensure that the person you love is protected by a guardianship arrangement that truly meets their needs.

sections.heading: Navigating Complex Proceedings
paragraphs: Guardianship proceedings involve probate courts and specific procedural requirements. Our experience ensures the process is handled correctly and efficiently.

sections.heading: Compassionate Guidance
paragraphs: We understand that seeking guardianship is often a sign of a difficult family situation. We handle these cases with the sensitivity and compassion they deserve.

items.title: Modifications
items.heroTitle: Order Modification Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Updating custody, support, and possession orders when life changes.

paragraphs: Life changes. A court order that was fair and appropriate when it was signed may no longer reflect the current reality of your family's situation. Texas law provides a legal mechanism for modifying court orders, but only when the right legal standard is met. As your modification attorney in Houston, Hirani Law Firm helps clients understand when a modification is legally possible and fights to achieve the best possible outcome for their updated circumstances.

sections.heading: Child Custody & Conservatorship
paragraphs: Modifications to conservatorship and the right to designate the primary residence of a child are among the most significant modifications possible. They require meeting a high legal standard.

sections.heading: Child Support
paragraphs: Both upward and downward modifications of child support are possible when there has been a significant change in either parent's income or the child's needs.

sections.heading: Visitation / Possession Schedule
paragraphs: A possession schedule can be modified to better accommodate the schedules of the parents and the needs of the children, provided the legal standard is met.

sections.heading: Spousal Support
paragraphs: Spousal maintenance orders can often be modified or terminated when the circumstances of either party change significantly.

sections.heading: Triggering Events for Child Custody Modifications
paragraphs: Common triggering events for a custody modification include: a parent relocating (or threatening to relocate); a parent's living situation or marital status changing; evidence of abuse, neglect, or substance abuse; the child's expressed preference (if 12 or older); or a parent's failure to comply with the existing order.

sections.heading: Triggering Events for Child Support Modifications
paragraphs: Common triggering events for a child support modification include: a significant increase or decrease in either parent's income (generally 20% or more); a change in the child's healthcare needs; a change in the primary residence of the child; or it has been three years since the last order and the amount would be different by 20% or $100 if calculated today.

sections.heading: Filing the Petition
paragraphs: The modification process begins with filing a Petition to Modify the Parent-Child Relationship or Petition to Modify Child Support with the appropriate court.

sections.heading: Temporary Orders
paragraphs: In urgent situations — such as when a child's safety is at risk — we can request Temporary Orders from the court that take effect immediately while the modification case is pending.

sections.heading: Negotiation or Trial
paragraphs: Like the original order, a modification can be reached through agreement between the parties or, if no agreement can be reached, through a contested hearing before a judge.

sections.heading: Responsive Advocacy
paragraphs: We move quickly to address changes in your circumstances and file for modification promptly so you are not waiting in a situation that is no longer appropriate.

sections.heading: Protecting Your Children
paragraphs: When circumstances change, children are often the most affected. We fight for modification outcomes that put your children's current best interests first.

sections.heading: Efficient Process Management
paragraphs: We manage the modification process efficiently, keeping your costs down while fighting effectively for the changes you need.

items.title: Enforcement & Contempt
items.heroTitle: Enforcement & Contempt Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Holding the other party accountable when a court order is ignored.

paragraphs: A court order is not a suggestion; it is a legally binding directive. When the other party in your family law case refuses to pay child support, denies you court-ordered visitation, or fails to comply with any other provision of your divorce decree or custody order, they are violating the law. As your enforcement attorney in Houston, Hirani Law Firm acts quickly and decisively to compel compliance and hold the violating party accountable.

sections.heading: Filing a Motion for Enforcement
paragraphs: When a court order is being violated, the remedy is to file a Motion for Enforcement with the court. This initiates a hearing where the other party must appear before a judge and explain their non-compliance.

sections.heading: Contempt of Court
paragraphs: If a judge finds that a party willfully violated a court order, they can be held in contempt of court. This is a serious legal finding with significant consequences.

sections.heading: Consequences of Contempt
paragraphs: A finding of contempt can result in fines, payment of the other party's attorney's fees, and in cases of ongoing or deliberate non-compliance, incarceration in the county jail.

sections.heading: Child Support Enforcement
paragraphs: If the other parent is not paying court-ordered child support, we file immediately. Courts take child support non-payment very seriously, and we pursue all available remedies, including wage withholding, license suspension, and contempt.

sections.heading: Child Custody & Visitation Enforcement
paragraphs: If you are being denied your court-ordered time with your children, or if the other parent is consistently failing to exercise their visitation (interfering with your children's relationship), we can take legal action to enforce the order and potentially seek a modification.

sections.heading: Property Division Enforcement
paragraphs: If your ex-spouse has failed to transfer property, close accounts, or fulfill other obligations from the divorce decree, we file an enforcement action to compel compliance.

sections.heading: Spousal Support Enforcement
paragraphs: If your ex-spouse is not making court-ordered alimony payments, we file to enforce the obligation and recover any arrearages owed.

sections.heading: Challenging the Allegations
paragraphs: If you have been served with an enforcement motion, we immediately analyze the allegations to identify any defenses available to you.

sections.heading: Providing Justification
paragraphs: Sometimes non-compliance has a legitimate reason, such as a sudden job loss. We present your circumstances to the court in the most favorable light and work to find a solution that avoids harsh penalties.

sections.heading: Negotiating a Resolution
paragraphs: In many cases, enforcement disputes can be resolved through negotiation without a full contested hearing. We work to find a practical solution while protecting your rights.

sections.heading: Tenacious Advocacy
paragraphs: Whether we are filing enforcement or defending against it, we are relentless advocates for our clients.

sections.heading: Knowledge of Local Courts
paragraphs: Our experience in Harris County and Fort Bend County courts gives us an advantage in understanding how local judges handle enforcement matters.

sections.heading: Protecting Your Rights on Both Sides
paragraphs: We represent clients both filing enforcement actions and defending against them.

items.title: Property Division
items.heroTitle: Property Division Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Protecting your fair share of the marital estate in a Texas divorce.

paragraphs: How your marital assets and debts are divided in a divorce will have a profound and lasting impact on your financial future. Texas community property law is complex, and the difference between a good property division settlement and a poor one can be hundreds of thousands of dollars. As your property division attorney in Houston, Hirani Law Firm is committed to ensuring you receive every dollar you are entitled to.

sections.heading: Community Property (Marital Property)
paragraphs: In Texas, all property acquired by either spouse during the marriage is presumed to be community property, owned equally by both. This includes income, real estate, vehicles, retirement accounts accrued during the marriage, and most other assets acquired after the wedding date.

sections.heading: Separate Property
paragraphs: Separate property is property that belongs solely to one spouse. This generally includes: property owned before the marriage; gifts and inheritances received during the marriage; and certain personal injury settlements. Separate property is not subject to division in a divorce.

sections.heading: Tracing Separate Property
paragraphs: The presumption is always that property is community property. To overcome this presumption and protect your separate property, you must 'trace' the asset — meaning you must provide clear evidence showing it originated from a separate source. This often requires detailed financial records and expert analysis.

sections.heading: Homes & Real Estate
paragraphs: The marital home is often a couple's largest asset. We help clients navigate the complex decision of whether to sell the home and divide the proceeds, or for one spouse to buy out the other's interest, including addressing the mortgage.

sections.heading: Business Interests & Professional Practices
paragraphs: Business interests are among the most complex and contentious assets to divide. We work with business valuation experts to determine the accurate value of any business and fight for your fair share, whether you are the owner or the non-owner spouse.

sections.heading: Retirement Accounts & Pensions (QDROs)
paragraphs: Dividing retirement accounts requires specialized legal orders. A Qualified Domestic Relations Order (QDRO) is a specific court order required to divide 401(k)s, pensions, and other qualified retirement plans. Failure to obtain a proper QDRO can result in tax penalties and the loss of the asset.

sections.heading: Stock Options, RSUs, and Investment Accounts
paragraphs: Stock options and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) are valuable and complex assets. We analyze vesting schedules to determine what portion is community vs. separate property and negotiate for a fair division.

sections.heading: Hidden Assets
paragraphs: Some spouses attempt to hide assets before or during a divorce. We are experienced at identifying warning signs of hidden assets and using legal discovery tools — including subpoenas, depositions, and forensic accountants — to uncover them.

sections.heading: Debts
paragraphs: Property division includes the division of marital debts, not just assets. We ensure that the debt assigned to each party is fair and that our clients are protected from the other spouse's failure to pay.

sections.heading: Protecting Your Business
paragraphs: If you own a business, protecting it from being divided or overvalued in a divorce is a primary concern. We develop strategies to protect business interests while still achieving a fair overall settlement.

sections.heading: Uncovering Hidden Assets
paragraphs: We do not take financial disclosures at face value. Our firm knows how to investigate and uncover assets that have been concealed, undervalued, or transferred to third parties.

sections.heading: Working with Financial Experts
paragraphs: For complex divorces involving significant assets, we collaborate with Certified Divorce Financial Analysts (CDFAs), forensic accountants, and business valuation experts to build a complete and accurate financial picture.

sections.heading: Strategic Negotiation & Trial Readiness
paragraphs: We negotiate aggressively for a fair settlement and are fully prepared to present a detailed, expert-supported case to a judge if negotiations fail.

items.title: Prenuptial Agreements
items.heroTitle: Prenuptial Agreement Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Thoughtful premarital agreements that protect both partners.

paragraphs: Discussing a prenuptial agreement can feel unromantic, but it is one of the most practical and loving things you can do before entering a marriage. A well-drafted prenuptial agreement protects both parties, sets clear expectations, and can actually prevent the most bitter conflicts in the event of a divorce. As your prenuptial and marital agreement attorney in Houston, Hirani Law Firm helps couples create clear, legally enforceable agreements that protect their individual interests and lay a strong foundation for their future together.

sections.heading: Key Provisions in a Prenup
paragraphs: A prenuptial agreement can address a wide range of financial matters, including: the characterization of property as separate or community; how property will be divided in the event of a divorce; spousal support obligations (or the waiver of them); the disposition of a family business; protection of an inheritance or family trust; and the management of finances during the marriage.

sections.heading: What a Prenup Cannot Do
paragraphs: There are important limitations. A prenuptial agreement cannot include provisions that: determine child custody or child support in advance (courts will not enforce these, as the child's best interest must be determined at the time of divorce); are illegal; or are unconscionable.

sections.heading: Protecting Your Business
paragraphs: If you own a business before you marry, a prenuptial agreement is one of the most important tools for ensuring that your business remains your separate property and is not subject to division if the marriage ends.

sections.heading: Protecting Inheritances
paragraphs: If you expect to receive a significant inheritance, a prenuptial agreement can ensure that inheritance remains your separate property and protects the interests of children from a prior relationship.

sections.heading: Protecting Against Debt
paragraphs: If your future spouse comes into the marriage with significant debt, a prenuptial agreement can protect you from becoming responsible for those obligations.

sections.heading: Clarity and Fairness
paragraphs: A well-drafted prenuptial agreement creates clarity about financial expectations and can actually reduce conflict by establishing rules in advance. Both parties must enter the agreement fully and voluntarily.

sections.heading: Grounds for Invalidity
paragraphs: Texas courts can invalidate a prenuptial agreement that was: not in writing; not signed voluntarily (signed under duress or coercion); not executed before the marriage; based on fraud or misrepresentation; or unconscionable at the time of signing.

sections.heading: Protecting Your Agreement's Validity
paragraphs: For an agreement to hold up in court, both parties must make full financial disclosure and have an opportunity to consult with independent legal counsel. Having separate attorneys for each party dramatically increases the likelihood of enforceability.

sections.heading: Drafting Enforceable Agreements
paragraphs: We draft agreements that are carefully worded to withstand legal scrutiny, ensuring all formal requirements are met.

sections.heading: Honest Conversations
paragraphs: We guide our clients through difficult financial conversations in a structured and productive way, ensuring both parties understand what they are agreeing to.

sections.heading: Protecting Both Parties
paragraphs: We believe the best prenuptial agreements are ones that are fair to both parties. An agreement that is grossly one-sided is more likely to be challenged and invalidated.

You are hurting, you're recovering, and now you're staring down medical bills while wondering how you'll pay for daily expenses. When you are injured on someone else's grounds, the law protects your right to recover damages under Texas premises liability law.

items.title: Workers' Compensation
items.heroTitle: Workplace Injury Attorney in Houston & Katy, TX
items.heroSubtitle: Help for injured workers facing denied benefits and disputed claims.

paragraphs: Hurt on the Job? We're Your Advocates for Workers Compensation Benefits. If you've been injured while on the job, securing fair workers compensation benefits should not be another fight. We are here to guide you through the process, providing the experienced and compassionate representation you need to protect your future.

sections.heading: Texas Work Injury System Overview
paragraphs: The Texas worker compensation system is the only one in the nation that allows private employers to opt out of state worker comp insurance. This unique rule means that when you suffer an injury, you typically fall into one of two complex legal paths:

sections.heading: Subscriber Claims (The DWC Route)
paragraphs: If your employer subscribes to the state system, your claim is 'no-fault.' While you don't have to prove employer negligence to receive benefits, you generally cannot sue your employer. Common issues we handle include:
bullets: Denied Claims: Many valid worker comp claims are initially denied. If you receive a denial notice, you have a short window to appeal. Without a skilled worker comp appeal lawyer, securing earned benefits is challenging.
Fighting for Treatment: Insurers often try to control medical decisions, delaying necessary care or disputing the severity of your occupational injury.
Worry over Lost Wages: We fight disputes over lost wages claim payments, like Temporary total disability (TTD) benefits, so you can focus on healing.

sections.heading: Non-Subscriber Lawsuits
paragraphs: If your employer is a non-subscriber (meaning they do not carry state worker compensation insurance), your legal path changes entirely. The employer loses crucial common-law defenses and is exposed to a personal injury lawsuit.
Whether your case involves an industrial accident in Houston or a repetitive stress injury, we ensure your rights as an injured worker are protected against the employer or their private plan.

sections.heading: Suing a Non-Subscriber Employer
paragraphs: When we file a suit against a non-subscriber employer, we must prove that the employer's negligence caused your injury. Because they opted out of the state system, they forfeit most defenses. This means we can seek a full recovery for all damages, including medical bills, 100% of lost wages, future earning capacity, and compensation for pain and suffering damages unavailable in standard worker comp claims. This path offers a chance at full justice.

sections.heading: Pursuing a Third-Party Lawsuit
paragraphs: Even if your employer is a subscriber, you may have grounds for a third-party lawsuit against another entity whose negligence contributed to your injury. Examples often include:
bullets: A negligent contractor or subcontractor on a job site.
A property owner (if the injury occurred at a third-party site).

sections.heading: Firm Philosophy
paragraphs: At Hirani Law Firm PLLC, meticulous legal preparation and deep compassion go hand-in-hand. We are a dedicated worker comp law firm ready to represent you.

Attorney Sehar Hirani's foundation in family law, guiding clients through life's most difficult times, means we approach every work injury case with the same commitment to unwavering compassion and meticulous preparation. We understand that an on-the-job injury is a family crisis, and we apply that care to ensure personal injury victims receive justice.

sections.heading: Services Provided
paragraphs: As your Houston worker compensation attorney, we manage every detail of your case:
bullets: Initial Claim Filing and Notice: We ensure proper injury notice is given and handle filing with the Texas Department of Insurance, preventing missed statute of limitations.
Contesting Denials: We immediately file appeals for any denied worker comp claim and prepare for the Benefit disputes / contested case hearing.

The Impairment Battle: We manage disputes over your Maximum Medical Improvement (MMI) date and Impairment rating (IR), ensuring proper documentation for your Permanent partial disability (PPD) benefits.
IME Preparation: We prepare you for any Independent Medical Examination (IME) requested by the insurer and challenge unfairly low ratings.
Complex Work Injuries: We have experience handling specialized claims like construction accident, oilfield injury sites, and warehouse injury situations.
Securing a Fair Settlement: We negotiate a lump sum settlement or prepare your case for trial, maximizing your worker comp settlement or full damages in an employer liability lawsuit.

sections.heading: Industry Expertise
paragraphs: The Houston and Katy areas are hubs for high-risk employment. We bring targeted experience to industries where accidents are frequent:
bullets: Energy and Oilfield: We represent workers injured in explosions, equipment malfunctions, and falls specific to the energy sector. We understand the unique liability issues in oilfield workers compensation cases.
Construction and Industrial Sites: We aggressively pursue compensation for falls, crane accidents, and heavy machinery injuries common in construction accident cases.
Transportation and Logistics: We help logistics workers and truck driver injury workers compensation clients recover income benefits after trauma or repetitive stress injury.
